title: Leissing v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The complaint was sustained by reference to Issue 5 of Case 2008-15. Presbytery's November 7 action dissolving the calls of REs Linton and Pellom, and the related Sealy Commission proceedings, were voided.
first_summary: Leissing challenged Presbytery's reversal of its Sealy Commission and resulting dissolution of the calls of REs Linton and Pellom. By reference to Case 2008-15, the SJC held that Presbytery had erred in appointing the Commission because the August 7 congregational meeting produced no valid dissolution request. The related actions were therefore voided.
summary: Leissing challenged Presbytery's November 7 action dissolving the calls of REs Linton and Pellom. By reference to Case 2008-15, the SJC sustained the complaint: the Session had canceled the August 7 congregational meeting, so it generated no valid dissolution request and Presbytery erred in appointing the Sealy Commission. The Commission proceedings, the complaint against its decision, and Presbytery's resulting dissolution action were voided; absent subsequent congregational action, the elders' calls remained undissolved.
